metadata.architecture: unnormalized scalar residual causal decoder with affine tied readout
metadata.author: anadim, declarative experiment wrapper
metadata.mechanism_hypothesis: An unnormalized scalar residual can encode arithmetic state continuously, while class-specific readout biases let tied scalar logits discriminate all tokens.
metadata.name: Scalar Affine Residual Attention Adder
metadata.research_current_explanation: The width-2 parent retained visible fitness 3 without an execution failure, so severe compression appears structurally viable. No visible accuracy gain establishes that normalized two-dimensional states are necessary.
metadata.research_evidence: Visible history reports execution, transformer validity, and eligibility for the earlier decoder but zero public accuracy; the compressed parent subsequently retained fitness 3.
metadata.research_next_experiment: Test an unnormalized width-1 residual causal-attention stream with tied embedding weights and a trainable 15-class readout bias.
metadata.research_expected_result: The scalar stream should reduce trusted parameter count while preserving eligibility, and affine class biases should avoid restricting predictions to only the extrema of a bias-free scalar codebook.
metadata.research_decision_rule: Reject the candidate if it loses public eligibility; otherwise prefer the lower trusted parameter count, using public accuracy only for an exact parameter-count tie.
metadata.research_previous_interpretation: The width-2 result supports compression as an eligibility-preserving direction, but it provides no decisive evidence that parameter-free normalization or vector-valued logits help addition.
metadata.research_challenged_assumption: The current direction assumes at least two normalized hidden coordinates are needed to distinguish the 15 output tokens.
metadata.research_alternative_explanation: A continuous scalar arithmetic state may suffice if each tied token logit has its own intercept, producing multiple decision intervals along the scalar axis.
metadata.research_discriminating_evidence: Eligibility with a lower trusted parameter count favors the scalar affine explanation, and nonzero public accuracy strengthens it; invalidity or loss of eligibility favors the normalized vector-state assumption.
